At some West Virginia DMV locations, they’re conducting closed-circuit driver’s tests.

For some closed-circuit tests in West Virginia, it will simply be slow speed manoeuvres (parallel parking, backing into a parking space, and driving around cones); for others, it will be a mini-driving course.
SHORTENED TEST
In 2022, the state of West Virginia is doing a shortened driver's test for the most part.
This means that rather than a 15-30 minute on-road driver's test, the test is now 8-15 minutes.

Be sure to back in to the parking space at West Virginia DMV at the beginning of your driver’s test, unless signs prohibit backing in.
When leaving at the beginning of your test, be sure to signal in the direction you’re going when you leave the parking space.
When you return to the DMV, know that you’re going to have to back into the parking space (reverse stall parking.)
